To accept non-standard assets (i.e., assets not considered to have low credit, liquidity and market risks), a Recognised Clearing House is expected to set and enforce appropriately conservative haircuts and concentration limits and to have appropriate collateral risk management procedures in place. [PID:10::4.10.2.Guidance]

[PID:10::4.10.3]

At a minimum, the system must: enable timely margin calls, accurate daily reporting of initial and variation margin, and dispute management; track collateral reuse and the clearing house’s rights to collateral; support timely deposit, withdrawal, substitution and liquidation; adjust acceptable collateral requirements as risks change; use prudent valuation practices including daily mark-to-market; develop haircuts that are regularly tested and independently validated at least annually and reflect stressed conditions (and aim to reduce procyclicality via stable, conservative haircuts calibrated to stressed periods); apply concentration limits (or concentration charges) that are periodically reviewed; and, where collateral is held in another jurisdiction or under non-ADGM law, mitigate associated FX, legal and operational risks to ensure timely usability and address significant liquidity and legal risks. [PID:10::4.10.3]
